entities.summary: Natural phenomenon when daylight lasts for more than 24 hours, occurring only inside or close to the polar circles, such as in the Arctic and subarctic regions of the Northern Hemisphere, including Alaska, Canada, Greenland, Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Russia. This phenomenon is caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis, which allows the sun to remain visible at midnight during the summer months. The midnight sun occurs when the sun is above the horizon for at least 24 hours, and it is most commonly observed in areas within the Arctic Circle, where the sun does not set below the horizon for at least one day in the summer. The midnight sun has been an important factor in the history of human settlement and exploration in the Arctic regions, as it has allowed people to live and work in areas that would otherwise be inhospitable due to the lack of sunlight. The midnight sun has also had a significant impact on the environment and ecosystems of the Arctic regions, as it allows for the growth of vegetation and the presence of certain animal species that are adapted to the unique conditions of the midnight sun.
